title: Multitasking exists because a clock keeps interrupting
body: Preemptive multitasking is a hardware timer periodically interrupting whatever runs, handing control to the kernel, which may resume something else. Programs need not cooperate; the clock guarantees nobody hogs the machine forever. Your editor and a runaway loop coexist because a crystal ticks against both of them.
source_hint: Computer architecture texts on timer interrupts and preemption
